transcript: y'all, Michael Arden has done it again. he, I mean, he really is just the master at reinventing classic stories and just new and unexpected ways. and that's exactly what he does with this production of A Christmas Carol, which is a one man production starring Jefferson Mays, who plays pretty much every character in the show um, it is the most visually stunning production. I've seen in a while, um, despite the fact that it is a one man production and those tend to be smaller scale standing set, um, this production goes all out on the production design. it's stunning set, um, props, lighting design, projection design, um, there's constant movement and the set changes in the most unexpected and fun ways and I won't spoil any of that for you. but I mean, it really is magical at times. what this production is able to accomplish with so little and so much of that needs to go to both Michael Arden, who directed it, obviously, and Jeff the Maze, who it just firing on all cylinders and manages to keep you engaged and for the entire 90 minutes and to inhabit all of these different characters. it's just so impressive what they're able to accomplish with the show. and I say that as someone who has no strong affinity for a Christmas Carol. I kind of feel like it's been done to death. I did not feel like we needed another production of it. I went to this production, begrudgingly, on November 8th, and I was like, I don't think I'm gonna enjoy this. and I walked out just completely blown away. I highly recommend seeing this production if you're in New York, if you can get to New York. it is a perfect production for the holiday season and getting you in the holiday spirit. it is visually stunning for anyone who loves the tech side of theater and it will blow you away. I highly recommend it. it's playing through, I think, January 1st at the Niedderlander Theater. go see it.
